summary: pyyi ships trojan python3.7 CLI that fetches and executes remote code and intercepts REPL input
details: The package advertises itself as a cryptography library (README documents a pyyi.generate_key() API) but pyyi/__init__.py only sets __version__; the real shipped surface is a console_scripts entry 'python3.7 = pyyi.cli:main' that typosquats the Python interpreter binary name on PATH. When invoked, cli.run_payload POSTs to a hardcoded remote host at /api/update, base64+gzip-decodes the response's 'payload' field, and runs it via exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec')) — full remote code execution on the installer's host whenever the shipped python3.7 command is run. The destination host list is not a plain literal: _ENC_NET stores a base64 blob plus a 16-byte hex XOR key (10b146714d76370ae262fe6154e7bc25) and _baked_hosts reconstructs the host(s) at runtime; a PY3_SERVER/PY2_SERVER env var can override. The same CLI reproduces the real Python banner and uses echo-off tty reads to silently capture bare single-token lines typed at the prompt, POSTing each candidate to the same C2 (op=2) as a 'password' and persisting it XOR-scrambled to ~/.python3.7/state.json via remember_word. The combination of a cover-story package description, a PATH-shadowing python3.7 trojan, runtime-reconstructed obfuscated C2, fetch-and-exec of attacker-supplied Python, and deliberate credential interception at a fake REPL is a remote-access trojan.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
